before:
The airport for the Iguazu Falls, 13 km from downtown Foz do Iguaçu, and named after the falls themselves. It is the arrival point for Iguaçu National Park and for the Itaipu Dam.

The operator has changed twice in quick succession, which is worth knowing if an older contact list is being used. Infraero ran it until CCR won a 30-year concession in April 2021. CCR rebranded as Motiva in April 2025, then sold its entire airport portfolio to the Mexican operator ASUR in November 2025, with the transaction completing on 31 August 2026. ASUR runs it now.

A regular bus service connects the airport to the city.

It opened on 7 January 1974, replacing an older airfield inside the national park that sat closer to town and closed when this one opened.
after:
The airport for the Iguazu Falls, 13 km from the centre of Foz do Iguaçu, and named after the falls themselves. It is the arrival point for Iguaçu National Park and for the Itaipu Dam.

The operator has changed name and owner in quick succession, worth knowing for older contact lists. CCR took over from Infraero in 2022. Motiva, as CCR is now called, agreed in November 2025 to sell its airports to the Mexican operator ASUR. ASUR took over on 1 September 2026.

A regular bus service connects the airport to the city.

It opened in 1974, replacing an older airfield.

claims.claim: ASUR took over on 1 September 2026
claims.note: Was 'with the transaction completing on 31 August 2026. ASUR runs it now.' Buyer and seller both announced the completion on 1 September 2026 ('announced today', 'nesta data', 'concluiu hoje'), and the airport operator's own release of that day says ASUR takes over the Brazilian operations 'from today'. H2FOZ reports it as Tuesday 1 September. Wikipedia's 31 August is contradicted by all of them. DECEA's live entry still names CCR Aeroportos as the aerodrome's operator and the airport's website still carries the Motiva name: the concession company is unchanged, its owner is ASUR.
